title: Turn 2 needs turn 1
spec: M12 · derive the next call, exit on a field
intro: One question about Greenfield Logistics, two tool calls. The second call's arguments did not come from you — they came out of the first call's result. That derivation is the loop.
foot: Run it for real: cd labs/M12-react-agent-loop/solution && python react_agent.py

steps.title: Turn 1 — everything it has is your sentence
narrative: You ask: "Find all UCC filings for Greenfield Logistics in New York." No filing number, because you do not have one — finding it is the job.

Claude picks search_filings and fills both arguments straight out of your text: debtor_name from the company you named, state from the state you named. This first hop is the easy one; every argument is a transcription.
The response comes back with stop_reason: "tool_use", which is the loop's instruction to run the tool and go round again — not to answer.
steps.youDo: Run python react_agent.py and read the [ACT] / [INPUT] pair before the observation scrolls past.

terminal.text: [QUERY] Find all UCC filings for Greenfield Logistics in New York

state.label: turn 1 · where each argument came from

steps.title: The observation carries the next call's arguments
narrative: The tool returns a filing record. Buried in it is "filing_number": "UCC-2024-NY-0012847" — a string that appears nowhere in your question and nowhere in the system prompt.

On turn 2 Claude calls get_filing_details with exactly that string. It could not have guessed it, and you could not have supplied it. The argument was derived from the observation, which is the entire reason this is a loop and not a single call.
Toggle Before / After and compare the two [INPUT] blocks. Turn 1's arguments came from a human; turn 2's came from the world.
steps.claudeSays: The loop appends the assistant's tool_use block and the tool_result to messages, then calls the API again. Turn 2 is the same request shape as turn 1 — the only difference is that the transcript now contains an answer.

after.title: AFTER — turn 2, argument from the observation

steps.title: It stops on a field, not on the words "I'm done"
narrative: Turn 3 comes back with stop_reason: "end_turn" and the loop returns the text. The exit condition in react_agent.py is one line — if response.stop_reason != "tool_use": — and it reads a protocol field, never the prose.

The anti-pattern the module wants dead is the alternative: scanning the response text for "I'm done" or "Here's your answer". The lab states the reason plainly: "The model's text is non-deterministic. It might say 'done' mid-conversation or forget to say it when actually finished."

Two failure modes, both bad: the agent halts halfway through a research task because it narrated a milestone, or it spins to max_turns because it finished politely without the magic phrase. stop_reason has neither problem.

terminal.text:
--- Turn 1 ---
  stop_reason: tool_use
  -> Tool call: lookup_filing({"filing_number": "UCC-2024-NY-0012847"}...)

--- Turn 2 ---
  stop_reason: tool_use
  -> Tool call: check_risk_profile({"entity_name": "Greenfield Logistics LLC"}...)

--- Turn 3 ---
  stop_reason: end_turn
  -> Task complete. Final response delivered.
stop_reason is the ONLY reliable termination signal.

before.title: BEFORE — parsing text for a phrase

lines: if "I'm done" in response.text or "Here's your answer" in response.text:
# halts on a narrated milestone; runs forever on a polite finish
# a field the API sets, not language the model chose

steps.title: What the loop still does not give you
narrative: The loop terminates correctly and derives its own arguments — and it is still four lines of control flow with no budget. max_turns=10 is the only ceiling, and hitting it returns the string "Agent did not produce a final response within max turns", which is a fallback, not a plan.

Note also what the lab tells you to verify. Not the wording — "Exact wording varies between runs since Claude generates natural language" — but the structure: tool calls happened, results were observed, the final answer cites specific filing numbers, and the run finished in 3-5 turns. Assert on the trace, never on the prose.

Every module after this one adds something the bare loop lacks: M13 plans before acting, M16 filters what enters, M18 grades what comes out, M26 puts a hook between the decision and the world. The loop is the skeleton, not the agent.
steps.youDo: Set max_turns=1 and re-run query 2 — the risk query needs a search and a calculate, so it hits the ceiling and returns the fallback string.
